title: Detecting AI-Generated Videos with Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: arXiv:2605.05895v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Modern AI-generated videos are photorealistic at the single-frame level, leaving inter-frame dynamics as the main remaining axis for detection. Existing detectors typically handle this temporal evidence in three ways: feeding the full frame sequence to a generic temporal backbone, reducing one dominant temporal cue to fixed video-level descriptors, or comparing temporal features to real-video statistics through a detection metric. These strategies degrade sharply under cross-generator evaluation, where artifact type and timescale vary across generators. On caption-paired benchmark, GenVidBench, we identify two signatures that prior detectors do not jointly exploit: AI-generated videos exhibit smoother frame-to-frame temporal residuals at the pixel level, and more compact trajectories in the semantic feature space, indicating a temporal smoothness gap at both levels. translated_abstract: 现代AI生成的视频在单帧层面已达到照片级的真实感，使得帧间动态成为检测的主要剩余依据。现有检测器通常以三种方式处理这种时间证据：将完整的帧序列输入通用的时间骨干网络，将单一的主要时间线索简化为固定的视频级描述符，或者通过检测度量将时间特征与真实视频的统计数据进行比较。这些策略在跨生成器评估中性能急剧下降，因为伪影类型和时间尺度在不同生成器之间各不相同。在配备字幕的基准数据集GenVidBench上，我们识别出两个先前检测器未能共同利用的特征：AI生成的视频在像素级别表现出更平滑的帧间时间残差，并且在语义特征空间中表现出更紧凑的轨迹，这表明在两个层面都存在时间平滑性差距。我们进一步观察到，当原始视频被输入到脉冲……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文发现AI生成视频在像素级帧间残差和语义特征轨迹上均存在时间平滑性特征，并利用脉冲神经网络对这一时间动态证据进行建模，以实现跨生成器的AI视频检测。
en_tdlr: This paper exploits two temporal smoothness signatures of AI-generated videos—smoother frame-to-frame pixel residuals and more compact semantic-space trajectories—and employs Spiking Neural Networks to detect them robustly across generators.
